# Asteroids

Atari's 1979 arcade game, with the same shapes, letters, sounds, motion and patterns.
Given the same controls, it plays the arcade's game frame for frame from power-on to the
end of the first game, checked against MAME's emulation: every value of the game's state
on every frame, and the vector picture the beam draws.

Keys: ← → or A S turn, ↑ or ' thrust, Space or Return fire, ↓ or / hyperspace, Return or
Space start, Escape pause.

The shape to notice:

- **The game is a dataset with its own rules.** `Game` in game.declare holds what is on
  the field as records — rocks, shots, saucer shots, the saucer and the ship — and the
  rest of the game as attributes, with a method per rule. `step` moves it all on by one
  frame.
- **Time enters as integration.** A frame `Time` moves the game on a frame at a time: in
  step with the display where its frames divide the arcade's 16 ms closely enough, as at
  60 Hz and its multiples, and every 16 ms of banked time on any other display.
- **The screen follows the data.** Views are replicated from the records the beam drew
  this frame; texts, scores and the sound board are constraints on the game's `mode`
  and state. Nothing in the views updates anything.
- **Everything is a whole number** in the arcade's own units, so the game is the same
  game every time.

What the beam draws is in art.declare: outlines, dots and letters decoded from the
arcade's vector ROM. The sound board is in sounds.declare: clips recorded from MAME's
emulation of the arcade's sound circuits. There is one player; "1 COIN 1 PLAY" is shown,
but one key starts a game. There is no list of high scores, between games or after one:
the high score at the top starts at 32460, and a game that ends with a better score
becomes it, where the arcade would ask for initials and then show its list. In an
explosion's first frames, the shrapnel can sit up to about four screen units from where
the arcade draws it.

*This program is new code, written in Declare. It recreates the behavior of Asteroids, Atari's
1979 arcade game, whose original program was written in 6502 assembly language, and reproduces
its look and sound as closely as it can, frame by frame. Asteroids, its name, artwork, sounds
and visual design belong to Atari, Inc. or its successors; they are used here only to
illustrate and test the Declare language, and no claim is made to them. The MIT license of this
repository covers this code, not the original game's name, artwork or sounds. If you hold
rights in this material and object to its being posted here, please open an issue on this
repository on GitHub, or message me there, and I will remove it.*

segments.html:
include [ "game.declare", "art.declare", "sounds.declare", "../touch-pad.declare" ]

defaultFlags [ render = canvas, accessibility = false ]

App [ appName = "Asteroids", fill = black,
    // the game's records start empty; powerOn fills them

    game: Game [ highScore = 32460 ] { { "rocks": [], "shots": [], "saucerShots": [],
        "saucer": { "inPlay": false, "size": "large", "x": 0, "y": 0, "vx": 0, "vy": 0, "blast": 0, "struck": false },
        "ship": { "state": "waiting", "x": 0, "y": 0, "vx": 0, "vy": 0, "heading": 0, "wait": 0,
            "landing": "safe", "blast": 0, "struck": false } } },
    sounds: SoundBoard [ game = { app.game }, paused = { app.paused } ],

    // the arcade's buttons, on the keyboard or the touch screen

    controls() -> Controls {
        return {
            left: Keys.isDown("ArrowLeft") || Keys.isDown("KeyA") || app.pad.isDown("left"),
            right: Keys.isDown("ArrowRight") || Keys.isDown("KeyS") || app.pad.isDown("right"),
            thrust: Keys.isDown("ArrowUp") || Keys.isDown("Quote") || app.pad.isDown("thrust"),
            fire: Keys.isDown("Space") || Keys.isDown("Enter") || app.pad.isDown("fire"),
            hyperspace: Keys.isDown("ArrowDown") || Keys.isDown("Slash") || app.pad.isDown("hyperspace"),
            start: Keys.isDown("Enter") || Keys.isDown("Space") || app.pad.isDown("start")
            }
        },

    // Escape pauses a game in play; any key goes on with it. The key that goes on also counts as
    // pressed, so a turn or thrust held to resume carries on at once.

    paused: boolean = false,

    // Keys go to the focused view, so a click or touch on the game gives it focus — needed
    // when a host runs it among other programs.

    focusable = true,
    onPointerDown() { Focus.focus(app) },

    keys: Keys [
        onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent) {
            app.restCursor()
            if (e.repeat || e.meta || e.ctrl || e.alt) return
            if (app.paused) app.paused = false
            else if (e.key == "Escape" && app.game.playing) app.paused = true
            }
        ],

    // In play the cursor is hidden over the game, and comes back when the game stops, when it
    // is paused, or when the mouse moves more than 10 pixels. A key hides it again.

    cursor = { (app.game.mode == "starting" || app.game.mode == "playing") && !app.paused && !app.mouseMoved
        ? "none" : "" },
    mouseMoved: boolean = false,
    restX: number = 0,                  // where the pointer was at the last key
    restY: number = 0,
    restCursor() { mouseMoved = false; restX = pointerX; restY = pointerY },
    trackChanges = ["pointerX", "pointerY"],
    onChange(e: ChangeEvent) {
        if (Math.abs(pointerX - restX) > 10 || Math.abs(pointerY - restY) > 10) mouseMoved = true
        },

    // The arcade moves the game on a frame every 16 ms. Where a whole number of the display's
    // frames comes within 5% of that, as at 60 Hz and its multiples, the game moves on every
    // that many display frames, so each of its frames is shown for the same time, and it runs
    // that much slower or faster than the arcade. On any other display, time banks between
    // display frames and the game moves on every 16 ms of it.

    clock: Time [ tick = frame, running = { !app.paused },
        frameTime: number = 0,          // the display's frame, averaged, in seconds
        shown: number = 0,              // display frames since the game last moved on
        banked: number = 0,
        onTick(dt: number) {
            for (let n = this.gameFrames(dt); n > 0; n--) app.game.step(app.controls())
            },
        gameFrames(dt: number) -> number {
            // a late frame stands for the display frames it covered, and stays out of the average
            if (frameTime == 0) frameTime = dt
            else if (dt < 1.5 * frameTime) frameTime = 0.95 * frameTime + 0.05 * dt
            const per = Math.max(1, Math.round(0.016 / frameTime))
            if (Math.abs(per * frameTime - 0.016) <= 0.05 * 0.016) {
                shown = shown + Math.max(1, Math.round(dt / frameTime))
                const n = Math.floor(shown / per)
                shown = shown - n * per
                return n
                }
            banked = banked + dt
            const n = Math.floor(banked / 0.016)
            banked = banked - n * 0.016
            return n
            }
        ],

    // What the beam drew this frame. It draws as things move, before hits are found: a rock
    // split off this frame is drawn from the next, and anything hit is drawn whole once more.

    drawn: Dataset [ schema = [ rocks[]: Rock, shots[]: Shot ],
        contents = { { rocks: app.game.value.rocks.filter((r) => r.drawn),
            shots: app.game.value.shots.concat(app.game.value.saucerShots).filter((s) => s.drawn) } } ],

    // The arcade's screen, scaled to fit the window.

    screen: View [ width = 1044, height = 788, clip = true,
        scale = { Math.min(app.width / width, app.height / height) },
        x = { (app.width - width * scale) / 2 },
        y = { (app.height - height * scale) / 2 },

        field: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%,
            rocks: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, datapath = { app.drawn.value },
                FieldFigure [ datapath = :rocks[], classFor = { :blast > 0 && !:struck ? Shrapnel : RockOutline } ],
                ShotDot [ datapath = :shots[] ]
                ],
            saucer: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, datapath = { app.game.value.saucer },
                SaucerOutline [ exists = { :inPlay && (:blast == 0 || :struck) } ],
                Shrapnel [ exists = { :inPlay && :blast > 0 && !:struck } ]
                ],
            ship: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, datapath = { app.game.value.ship },
                ShipOutline [ exists = { :state == "flying" || :struck }, flame = { app.game.flame } ],
                Wreck [ exists = { :state == "exploding" && !:struck }, debris = { app.game.debris } ]
                ]
            ],

        Score [ cx = 100, cy = 876, magnify = 2, points = { app.game.score } ],
        ReserveShips [ count = { app.game.shipsLeft } ],
        Score [ cx = 480, cy = 876, points = { app.game.highScore } ],
        Score [ cx = 768, cy = 876, magnify = 2, visible = { !app.game.playing } ],      // a second player's, between games

        // Between games: "1 COIN 1 PLAY" at the top, then how to start, and the controls in two
        // columns of small letters, the last of them on the line where the arcade itself shows
        // "1 COIN 1 PLAY". All are centered on the copyright's middle (490 across).

        ArcadeText [ cx = 338, cy = 792, magnify = 2, text = "1 COIN 1 PLAY", visible = { !app.game.playing } ],

        View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, visible = { app.game.mode == "attract" },
            ArcadeText [ cx = { app.touchFirst ? 358 : 242 }, cy = 372, magnify = 2,
                text = { app.touchFirst ? "PRESS START" : "PRESS RETURN TO START" } ],
            keyLines: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, visible = { !app.touchFirst },
                KeyLine [ cy = 324, action = "ROTATE LEFT", keys = "← OR A" ],
                KeyLine [ cy = 300, action = "ROTATE RIGHT", keys = "→ OR S" ],
                KeyLine [ cy = 276, action = "THRUST", keys = "↑ OR '" ],
                KeyLine [ cy = 252, action = "FIRE", keys = "RETURN OR SPACE" ],
                KeyLine [ cy = 228, action = "HYPERSPACE", keys = "↓ OR /" ]
                ]
            ],
        ArcadeText [ cx = 400, cy = 728, magnify = 2, text = "PLAYER 1", visible = { app.game.mode == "starting" } ],
        ArcadeText [ cx = 400, cy = 628, magnify = 2, text = "GAME OVER", visible = { app.game.mode == "over" } ],
        Copyright [ ],

        // paused: the screen dimmed, and the word at full brightness where the arcade puts
        // its messages

        View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, fill = black, opacity = 0.6, visible = { app.paused } ],
        ArcadeText [ cx = 436, cy = 628, magnify = 2, intensity = 15, text = "PAUSED", visible = { app.paused } ]
        ],

    // On a touch screen, the arcade's buttons where its panel has them: the two that turn
    // under the left hand, thrust and fire under the right, hyperspace between them
    // (../touch-pad.declare).

    pad: TouchPad [ startShown = { !app.game.playing }, ink = #8C8C8C, startInk = white,
        fieldX = { app.screen.x }, fieldY = { app.screen.y },
        fieldW = { app.screen.width * app.screen.scale }, fieldH = { app.screen.height * app.screen.scale },
        middle = { app.screen.x + 499 * app.screen.scale },        // the copyright's middle: 490 screen units, plus the 10 a view's x adds
        keys = { [
            { id: "left", label: "ROTATE LEFT", icon: "ccw", side: "left", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "right", label: "ROTATE RIGHT", icon: "cw", side: "left", col: 1, row: 0 },
            { id: "hyperspace", label: "HYPER SPACE", side: "center", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "thrust", label: "THRUST", side: "right", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "fire", label: "FIRE", side: "right", col: 1, row: 0 }
            ] } ]
    ]
